title: Hepatic lobule: portal triad and sinusoidal anatomy
description: See portal triad, central vein, sinusoidal cells and the opposite directions of blood and bile.

questions.question: How does blood flow through a hepatic lobule?
questions.answer: Branches of the portal vein and hepatic artery feed sinusoids near portal tracts; blood then drains toward the central vein.

questions.question: Does bile flow in the same direction as blood in a liver lobule?
questions.answer: No. Hepatocytes secrete bile into canaliculi that move toward bile ducts in portal tracts, generally opposite the sinusoidal blood flow.

questions.question: What is the portal venule?
questions.answer: Small portal vein branch delivering nutrient-rich splanchnic blood to sinusoids. Function: Feeds liver parenchyma.

questions.question: Where is the interlobular bile duct located?
questions.answer: Cholangiocyte-lined duct traveling with arterial and portal venous branches. Function: Receives bile from canalicular/ductular route.

questions.question: What is the function of the central vein?
questions.answer: Function: Collects sinusoidal blood toward hepatic veins. Terminal hepatic venule at center of classical lobule.
